parsed.rationale: All five members — `AppleMusicService`, `BandcampService`, `SoundCloudService`, `SpotifyService`, `YouTubeMusicService` — are `type-alias-object` records in the same package (`MusicShareKit`) and the same directory (`Services/`), each with an empty `fields_or_signature` list and `shared_field_count: 1`. This means every file contributes exactly one structural slot (the aliased type itself) and those slots are identical across all five files. Maintaining five separate files for what is structurally the same declaration creates unnecessary surface area and will cause all five files to drift in lockstep whenever the aliased type changes. Consolidating them — either into a single generic typealias or a discriminated value type — eliminates the duplication while preserving the named service identities callers depend on.

specifics.proposed_action: Introduce a single generic or protocol-backed `MusicService` type (or a parameterized `typealias`) in `MusicShareKit` that replaces the five structurally identical `type-alias-object` declarations (`AppleMusicService`, `BandcampService`, `SoundCloudService`, `SpotifyService`, `YouTubeMusicService`). Because all five are `type-alias-object` kinds with no fields (`fields_or_signature: []`) and share exactly one structural slot (`shared_field_count: 1`), they are almost certainly all aliases to the same underlying concrete or generic type. The recommended change is: (1) inspect the aliased RHS type in each file; (2) if all five alias the same type, delete four of the five files and introduce a single canonical name (or an enum/struct with a `platform` discriminator); (3) if the RHS differs only by a generic parameter, introduce a single generic typealias `MusicService<Platform>` in a new file `Shared/MusicShareKit/Sources/MusicShareKit/Services/MusicService.swift` and replace each per-service file with a one-line specialisation, or delete them entirely if callers can use the generic form directly.
specifics.why_no_category_fits: The cluster signal is `exact-duplicates` on `type-alias-object` nodes, not on structs, classes, or functions. None of the named categories map cleanly: `extract-to-common` applies to duplicated concrete types, not to typealiases that are themselves the duplication; `generic-parameterization` is the closest fit but the schema targets functions/structs/classes, not typealiases; `pat-introduction` and `protocol-inheritance` are inapplicable because there are no protocol members. The action is a typealias consolidation, which the schema does not have a dedicated category for.
